patches.old:
After I had written down the commandments and parables of the shepherd, the angel of repentance, he came to me and said, “I want to show you everything the Holy Spirit showed you when it spoke with you in the form of the church. For that spirit is the Son of God.”[a]

2. “Because you were weaker in the flesh, it was not made clear to you through an angel. When you were strengthened through the Spirit and grew strong enough even to see an angel, then the building of the tower was revealed to you through the church.[b] You saw everything beautifully and reverently, as through a virgin. But now you see through an angel, though through the same Spirit.”

3. “You must learn everything more accurately from me.[c] For this purpose I was assigned by the glorious angel to dwell in your house, so that you might see everything with strength, without being frightened as before.”

4. He took me to Arcadia, to a breast-shaped mountain, seated me on its summit and showed me a great plain. Around the plain were twelve mountains, each different in appearance.

5. The first was black as soot. The second was bare, with no vegetation. The third was thorny and full of thistles.

6. The fourth had half-dried vegetation: green at the top but dry near the roots. Some plants became dry when the sun scorched them.[d]

7. The fifth mountain had green vegetation and was rough. The sixth was full of cracks, some small and some large. Vegetation grew in the cracks, but it was not very flourishing; instead, it looked withered.

8. The seventh mountain had cheerful vegetation, and the whole mountain flourished. Every kind of livestock and bird grazed on it. The more the animals and birds fed, the more the mountain’s vegetation flourished. The eighth mountain was full of springs, and every kind of the Lord’s creation drank from its springs.

9. The ninth mountain had no water at all and was completely desolate. It contained wild beasts and deadly creeping creatures that destroyed people.[e] The tenth mountain had very large trees and was entirely shaded. Sheep lay beneath the shelter, resting and chewing the cud.

10. The eleventh mountain was densely wooded. Its trees were laden with fruit, adorned with different kinds of fruit, so that anyone seeing them would want to eat their fruit.[f] The twelfth mountain was entirely white, with a cheerful appearance. The mountain itself was most beautiful.

    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: The source explicitly says “that spirit is the Son of God.” The draft retains that identification
      and the church’s visionary form without harmonizing the sentence to a later doctrinal formulation.
      Michigan loses about twelve lines across most of this opening and resumes near the identification’s
      end; it does not independently certify the complete sentence.
  - marker: b
    reason: textual_variant
    text: '“Even to see an angel” follows Hilgenfeld’s printed conjecture kai angelon, compared with Vulgata.
      Athos reads oi angeloi, “the angels”; alternative: “So that the angels could see you.” The papyrus’s
      corresponding singular-angel phrase is partly supplied and gives no preserved kai vote. The draft
      keeps the source’s narrated sequence of church and angel rather than silently reordering the revelations
      to smooth its difficulty. Athos’s corresponding Greek construction is grammatically disturbed; the
      alternative gives its possible sense rather than claiming a smooth identical clause.'
  - marker: c
    reason: textual_variant
    text: '“Learn everything more accurately from me” retains the working Athos reading. Michigan’s published
      wording has a seeing verb rather than learning, with much of the clause restored. Alternative sense:
      “You must see everything more accurately through me.” The title glorious angel is preserved without
      inventing a personal name.'
  - marker: d
    reason: textual_variant
    text: 'Athos additionally says after this description: “The mountain was very rough, having dry vegetation.”
      The working edition omits that sentence compared with the versions. Michigan’s surviving fourth/fifth-mountain
      transition lacks the extra dry-vegetation sentence and describes the fifth as very rough but green.
      The draft retains the working distinction, recording the Athos addition rather than silently losing
      it or shifting it to another mountain as certain text.'
  - marker: e
    reason: textual_variant
    text: 'The working Athos wording coordinates wild beasts and deadly creeping creatures. Michigan’s
      published wording can instead construe creeping as qualifying the beasts: alternative sense, “It
      contained deadly creeping beasts that destroyed people.” Nearby letters are damaged, and the English
      does not narrow all creeping creatures to one modern species.'
  - marker: f
    reason: textual_variant
    text: The printed working body has a fruit-laden adjective; Athos is reported with a nearby fruit-adjective
      variant. The sense of abundant, varied fruit is retained. Michigan loses thirteen or fourteen lines
      between the ninth mountain’s ending and the twelfth’s opening, so does not certify the complete
      eleventh-mountain paragraph. The twelfth’s final reflexive construction is a printed version-supported
      correction, not unanimous Greek wording.

    σε καὶ ἄγγελον ἰδεῖν, τότε μέν οὖν ἐφανερώθη σοι διὰ τῆς Ἐκκλησίας ἡ οἰκοδομὴ τοῦ πύργου· καλῶς καὶ
    σεμνῶς πάντα ὡς ὑπὸ παρθένου ἑώρακας. νῦν δὲ ὑπὸ ἀγγέλου βλέπεις, διὰ τοῦ αὐτοῦ μὲν πνεύματος· 3.

    τὸν οἶκόν σου κατοικῆσαι, ἵνα δυνατῶς πάντα ἴδῃς, μηδὲν δειλαινόμενος ὡς καὶ τὸ πρότερον. 4. καὶ ἀπήγαγέ

    μέγα, κύκλῳ δὲ τοῦ πεδίου ὄρη δώδεκα, ἄλλην καὶ ἄλλην ἰδέαν ἔχοντα τὰ ὄρη. 5. τὸ πρῶτον ἦν μέλαν ὡς
    ἀσβόλη· τὸ δὲ δεύτερον ψιλόν, βοτάνας μὴ ἔχον· τὸ δὲ τρίτον ἀκανθῶδες καὶ τριβόλων πλῆρες· 6. τὸ δὲ
    τέταρτον βοτάνας ἔχον ἡμιξήρους, τὰ μὲν ἐπάνω τῶν βοτανῶν χλωρά, τὰ δὲ πρὸς τὰς ῥίζας ξηρά· τινὲς
    δὲ βοτάναι, ὅταν ὁ ἥλιος ἐπικεκαύκει, ξηραὶ ἐγίνοντο· 7. τὸ δὲ πέμπτον ὄρος ἔχον βοτάνας χλωράς, καὶ
    τραχὺ ὄν. τὸ δὲ ἕκτον ὄρος σχισμῶν ὅλον ἔγεμεν, ὧν μὲν μικρῶν, ὧν δὲ μεγάλων· εἶχον δὲ βοτάνας αἱ

    εἶχε βοτάνας ἱλαράς, καὶ ὅλον τὸ ὄρος εὐθηνοῦν ἦν, καὶ πᾶν γένος κτηνῶν καὶ ὀρνέων ἐνέμοντο εἰς τὸ

    αὐτῷ θηρία καὶ ἑρπετὰ θανάσιμα, διαφθείροντα ἀνθρώπους. τὸ δὲ δέκατον ὄρος εἶχε δένδρα μέγιστα, καὶ
    ὅλον κατάσκιον ἦν, καὶ ὑπὸ τὴν σκέπην πρόβατα κατέκειντο ἀναπαυόμενα καὶ μαρυκώμενα. 10. τὸ δὲ ἑνδέκατον

translation:
  text: 'I had written down the shepherd’s commandments and parables. The shepherd, the angel of repentance,
    came to me and said, “I want to show you everything the Holy Spirit showed you when it spoke with
    you in the form of the church. That spirit is the Son of God.”[a]


    2. “You were weaker in the flesh, so it was not made clear to you through an angel. The Spirit strengthened
    you. When you were strong enough even to see an angel, the church revealed the building of the tower
    to you.[b] You saw everything beautifully and reverently, as through a virgin. Now an angel shows
    you, through the same Spirit.”


    3. “You must learn everything more accurately from me.[c] The glorious angel assigned me to live in
    your house for this purpose. You can then see everything with strength, without being frightened as
    before.”


    4. He took me to a breast-shaped mountain in Arcadia and seated me on its summit. He showed me a great
    plain. Twelve mountains surrounded it. Each looked different.


    5. The first mountain was black as soot. The second was bare, without vegetation. The third was thorny
    and full of thistles.


    6. The fourth had vegetation that was half dry. It was green at the top but dry near the roots. Some
    plants dried up when the sun scorched them.[d]


    7. The fifth mountain was rough, with green vegetation. The sixth was full of small and large cracks.
    Plants grew in them, but looked withered rather than flourishing.


    8. The seventh mountain had cheerful vegetation. The whole mountain flourished. All kinds of livestock
    and birds grazed there. The more they fed, the more the plants flourished. The eighth mountain was
    full of springs. Every kind of the Lord’s creation drank from them.


    9. The ninth mountain was completely desolate and had no water. Wild beasts and deadly creeping creatures
    there destroyed people.[e] The tenth had very large trees. It was entirely shaded. Sheep lay under
    the shelter, resting and chewing the cud.


    10. The eleventh mountain was thick with trees. They were full of different kinds of fruit. Anyone
    seeing them would want to eat their fruit.[f] The twelfth mountain was entirely white and looked cheerful.
    The mountain itself was most beautiful.'

  - marker: a
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: The source explicitly says “that spirit is the Son of God.” The draft retains that identification
      and the church’s visionary form without harmonizing the sentence to a later doctrinal formulation.
      Michigan loses about twelve lines across most of this opening and resumes near the identification’s
      end; it does not independently certify the complete sentence.
  - marker: b
    reason: textual_variant
    text: '“Even to see an angel” follows Hilgenfeld’s printed conjecture kai angelon, compared with Vulgata.
      Athos reads oi angeloi, “the angels”; alternative: “So that the angels could see you.” The papyrus’s
      corresponding singular-angel phrase is partly supplied and gives no preserved kai vote. The draft
      keeps the source’s narrated sequence of church and angel rather than silently reordering the revelations
      to smooth its difficulty. Athos’s corresponding Greek construction is grammatically disturbed; the
      alternative gives its possible sense rather than claiming a smooth identical clause.'
  - marker: c
    reason: textual_variant
    text: '“Learn everything more accurately from me” retains the working Athos reading. Michigan’s published
      wording has a seeing verb rather than learning, with much of the clause restored. Alternative sense:
      “You must see everything more accurately through me.” The title glorious angel is preserved without
      inventing a personal name.'
  - marker: d
    reason: textual_variant
    text: 'Athos additionally says after this description: “The mountain was very rough, having dry vegetation.”
      The working edition omits that sentence compared with the versions. Michigan’s surviving fourth/fifth-mountain
      transition lacks the extra dry-vegetation sentence and describes the fifth as very rough but green.
      The draft retains the working distinction, recording the Athos addition rather than silently losing
      it or shifting it to another mountain as certain text.'
  - marker: e
    reason: textual_variant
    text: 'The working Athos wording coordinates wild beasts and deadly creeping creatures. Michigan’s
      published wording can instead construe creeping as qualifying the beasts: alternative sense, “It
      contained deadly creeping beasts that destroyed people.” Nearby letters are damaged, and the English
      does not narrow all creeping creatures to one modern species.'
  - marker: f
    reason: textual_variant
    text: The printed working body has a fruit-laden adjective; Athos is reported with a nearby fruit-adjective
      variant. The sense of abundant, varied fruit is retained. Michigan loses thirteen or fourteen lines
      between the ninth mountain’s ending and the twelfth’s opening, so does not certify the complete
      eleventh-mountain paragraph. The twelfth’s final reflexive construction is a printed version-supported
      correction, not unanimous Greek wording.
